general_rules.description: Internal team (same domain) receives casual tone with no greeting or first-name-only greeting, no closing signature.
Code-switch between English and French with internal French-speaking colleagues (Léa, Inès), using 'tu' form and mixing languages within single emails.
External French contacts (enterprise, investors, government) receive formal or semi-formal French with 'vous' form and proper closings.
Investor/VC contacts (Marcus, Claire, Sarah) receive semi-formal English or French with 'Hi/Bonjour' greeting and first-name-only closing.
Use emoji sparingly in internal casual emails (👌, 🔥, 🚀, ⚠️) but never in formal external communications.
Enterprise/formal external contacts receive full signature block (name + title) only in formal register; semi-formal uses first name only.
Action-oriented structure: numbered lists, direct requests, and imperative tone with internal team; structured paragraphs with external stakeholders.
Ultra-short responses to internal colleagues ('just go 🚀', 'exactement ce que je pensais') signal trust and speed.
Investor updates and external pitches include specific metrics (CAC, LTV, burn rate, ARR) formatted as structured lists.
French formal register uses 'Bien cordialement' or 'Cordialement' as standard closing; never 'Amicalement' or casual variants.
